transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. AI. What brings you in today?

I'm having a really hard time staying in my seat at work and find myself constantly getting up when I'm supposed to be sitting. It's making it incredibly difficult to keep my daily tasks organized because I just can't seem to stay put.
Do you also have trouble paying close attention, making careless mistakes, or finishing tasks because you get distracted, or is it mainly the restlessness and impulsive behavior?

I actually experience both types of issues. Besides feeling constantly restless and sometimes blurting out answers, I struggle a lot with inattention, especially when it comes to organizing my tasks and activities. I also find myself frequently forgetting important things in my daily routine.
Have these attention and hyperactivity symptoms been present since childhood, before age 12?

Yes, absolutely. I've struggled with these issues for as long as I can remember, definitely since before I was 12 years old. Even back in elementary school, my teachers were always complaining about me not staying in my seat.

latest_inference.note: Previously the only candidate was Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation), and the interview now strongly supports it rather than changing the differential. The patient reports both inattentive symptoms (disorganization, forgetfulness) and hyperactive/impulsive symptoms (restlessness, leaving seat, blurting out answers), with onset before age 12 and persistence since childhood, which fits the combined presentation. No evidence has emerged for an alternative diagnosis, so the candidate list remains the same.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports persistent symptoms of both inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity, including difficulty staying seated, restlessness, blurting out answers, disorganization, and forgetfulness. Symptoms began in childhood before age 12 and have continued into adulthood, which is most consistent with ADHD, combined presentation.
